report.summary: Source-only review of the five-file packet against the proposed cycle-22 revision-audit feature, which was pre-implementation. The packet has no history endpoint, no v1/v2 dispatcher in Root, no shared verifier path, and no new evidence-download button. The proposals cannot be judged as shipped, so findings focus on the proposed design. The strongest is the archive projection in proof-store.ts: archived versions have files, acceptanceEvidence, modelReport/history and modelArchive/history removed, which makes the proposed 'full retained files + per-version existing EvidenceBundle' replay impossible for archived versions. Other findings are the same-sequence/ambiguous-current selection (line 124), the 4 MiB vs 8 MiB core bound (evidence-export.ts line 29), and the aggregate cap ordering. I did not execute any check. Line numbers come only from the supplied sourceWithLineNumbers.

findings.title: Archived versions have no files, acceptance evidence or model archive, so the proposed per-version EvidenceBundle cannot be rebuilt for history
findings.evidence: listProofVersions reads proof_versions with json_remove stripping '$.delivery.files', '$.delivery.acceptanceEvidence', '$.delivery.modelReport', '$.delivery.modelHistory', '$.delivery.modelArchive' and modelEvidenceReservation. The wrote path at line 98 also stores the snapshot after dehydrateModelDelivery(snapshot.delivery) and delete snapshot.delivery.supplementalCatalog. readProofVersion (line 157-158) hydrates only model delivery objects, not files or acceptance snapshots. createEvidenceBundle (evidence-bundle.ts:76-89) calls createEvidenceExport, whose exportFiles (evidence-export.ts:71-80) and verifyEvidenceExport 'structure' check (line 262) require bundle.delivery.files to be a complete inventory. verifyEvidenceExport acceptance-references (lines 369-418) needs retention of delivery.acceptanceEvidence for snapshots and acceptanceReferences. The cycle proposal says the old delivery archive keeps 'exact createEvidenceExport core' with full files. The DB rows this function returns cannot support that.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted trace: deliver version A (v1), then accept it so acceptanceEvidence and a model archive exist, then save version B with archive:true. The INSERT at proof-store.ts:99-100 stores snapshot A after line 98 removes supplementalCatalog and the model archive is dehydrated. Later a GET of the proposed revision audit reads version A via this path. files, acceptanceEvidence, modelReport/modelHistory/modelArchive are absent. createEvidenceExport throws 'A current proof delivery is required' only if delivery is missing. Otherwise exportFiles/validateStaticFiles fails on missing files, and the acceptance-references check cannot find snapshots. The verifier reports inconsistent, or the endpoint silently drops the core and violates 'full retained files'.
findings.suggestion: Before implementing the audit, change snapshotVersion/saveProofCase so archived proof_versions keep delivery.files, acceptanceEvidence and the model archive needed by createEvidenceExport (or add a dedicated append-only raw snapshot table). Do not strip those fields in the json_remove projections for the audit path. Alternative, narrow version: state in the proposal that archived cores are not reconstructible and that the cycle-22 audit scope covers only files that actually exist in the archive, with the verifier reporting missing objects as inconsistent.

findings.title: Same-second archives and the prepended current row make version order ambiguous and can break 'current-last'
findings.evidence: The projection orders by desc(proofVersions.archivedAt) only. archivedAt is an ISO timestamp produced at saveProofCase time (line 91 `at = new Date().toISOString()`). Two versions saved in the same millisecond (seconds on some runtimes) have no tiebreaker, such as delivery.id or a monotonic sequence. listProofVersions then does list.unshift(current) (line 148) after the archived rows. So the proposed traversal '2-5 selected unique ordered versions, same project, current last' has to rely on an unstable second ordering. The proposed deterministic-rule checks (sequence uniqueness/monotonic, exact stale version) would then either reject a valid history or accept an arbitrary order.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted: freeze the clock or call saveProofCase twice quickly with archive:true for versions A and B. Both rows get the same archived_at. The SQL ORDER BY is then implementation-defined between A and B. The response is current-unshifted plus an arbitrary archived order. A consumer replaying rules with sequence ≤ previous or with planKey continuity would get inconsistent results for the same data on different queries.
findings.suggestion: Add a deterministic total order: ORDER BY archivedAt DESC, delivery.id DESC (or an explicit archived sequence column), and derive 'current last' from an explicit isCurrent flag plus the persisted delivery.sequence, not from list.unshift. Version selection (2-5 contiguous versions ending at current) should be computed server-side from that persisted order and returned with the same ordering key.

findings.title: Core export bound is 4 MiB while the bundle bound is 8 MiB, so the audit's 'full files + full core per version' aggregate can never exceed one core's replayable size without a separate, later budget
findings.evidence: EVIDENCE_EXPORT_BYTE_LIMIT is 4*1024*1024. boundedJson (line 105) rejects anything over that, in createEvidenceExport (line 139) and verifyEvidenceExport (line 250). EVIDENCE_BUNDLE_BYTE_LIMIT in evidence-bundle.ts:15 is 8 MiB, and assertEvidenceBundleBudget runs on the whole bundle (evidence-bundle.ts:52). For a current core already near 4 MiB, two versions (full files + core + supplemental per version) exceed 8 MiB immediately. The proposal says '8 MiB aggregate caps' plus 'full retained files + per-version existing EvidenceBundle'. These two requirements contradict each other for any project with large files, and the 2-5 version count cannot be honored.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted: a delivery with a 3.5 MiB HTML file. Its v2 createEvidenceBundle passes the 8 MiB bundle limit only if the core is under 4 MiB. A two-version audit (v1 core 3.5 MiB + v2 core 3.5 MiB + supplemental + diffs) is about 7 MiB plus overhead. Three versions exceed 8 MiB. The endpoint must then either truncate (forbidden by budget errors) or refuse a valid 3-version history that the proposal promises.
findings.suggestion: Define the audit budget explicitly: keep each core at its 4 MiB limit and size the revision-document limit from selected versions (for example, refuse with a typed error when per-version cores exceed the aggregate). Or stream a per-version document instead of embedding cores for a single 8 MiB body. State the limit in the proposal and in the verifier's limits object.

findings.title: Acceptance decisions are checked with an error-swallowing `check`, so catalogValid/acceptanceValid can be true even though their failing check was swallowed, and follow-up catalog fallbacks then depend on that state
findings.evidence: `check` (line 110) catches every failure and records the check as inconsistent. It does not throw. The outer verify only sets result.consistency and returns. Later, followup-bindings (lines 166-181) builds retainedRows with `catalogValid?...:[]` and `acceptanceValid?...:[]`. tasksValid and objectsValid explicitly early-return on failure, but catalogValid and acceptanceValid are not used to return, and they are booleans rather than replayed results. If supplemental-acceptance fails after catalogValid succeeded, legacy follow-up observations fall back to frozen catalogRows that no longer verify against any acceptance snapshot. The overall result is already inconsistent, so this cannot produce a false 'consistent'. However, the proposal asks to replay acceptance-critical supplemental decisions. A verifier that continues after cross-boundary failure makes that replay's failure semantics harder to state and audit.
findings.reproduction: Unexecuted logic trace: craft a bundle whose catalog rows re-derive correctly but whose acceptance snapshotSha256 is stale. `supplemental-acceptance` becomes inconsistent (result.consistency='inconsistent'), and the verifier continues into followup-bindings using catalogValid=true rows. The per-check messages are emitted separately, but there is no statement that acceptance-bound evidence is replayed from a consistent acceptance binding.
findings.suggestion: After catalogValid/acceptanceValid, skip the legacy retainedRows fallback unless acceptanceValid, or return early / require the checks that feed cross-boundary replay to pass before follow-up replay uses their outputs. Record that these checks short-circuit in the check messages.

limitations: Source-only review. No files changed, and no tool other than the required skill was used. All reproductions are reasoning traces labeled unexecuted.

The proposed cycle-22 revision-audit endpoint, the Root v1/v2 dispatcher, the verifier replay host and the EvidenceDownloads button are outside the packet. Their implementation, rate-limits, request-membership checks and CAS semantics cannot be reviewed.

Helper modules (supplemental-evidence, deployment-source, static-project, runtime-project) were not supplied, so their internals are treated as opaque and not reviewed.

No runtime, network, database or browser check was performed, and no live data or judge/opponent internals were inspected. The award comparison in the task is treated as the user-supplied official-strength summary, not as verified here.
